archetypes.name: shell-root-binding
archetypes.rationale: The plan hinges on a SCRIPT_ROOT-vs-PLUGIN_ROOT split that must be consistently applied across three different scripts; any inconsistency would silently repeat the original RC1 defect.
archetypes.prompt_body: Check that the plan's instructions on SCRIPT_ROOT vs PLUGIN_ROOT vs CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT are self-consistent across all modified files (upgrade-larch.sh, sessionstart-health.sh, and release/SKILL.md Step 7). Verify that lib-sparse-dirs.sh sourcing instructions each use the correct root binding as stated — SCRIPT_ROOT for the allowlist, PLUGIN_ROOT only for cache/stamp/prune context. Trace through the existing scripts (skills/upgrade-larch/scripts/upgrade-larch.sh lines 1–110 and scripts/sessionstart-health.sh) to confirm which variable names are already defined at each sourcing point and whether the plan's binding sequence could conflict with existing variable assignments. Flag any plan step where the allowlist would be sourced from the installed or cache root rather than the executing script tree, since that would silently repeat the original RC1 defect. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: release-root-resolution
archetypes.rationale: The RC1 fix embeds a 4-step CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT resolution chain in release/SKILL.md operator prose; gaps in that chain could leave the release calling a stale Skill-tool upgrade even on a standard marketplace install.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit the RC1 fix plan in .claude/skills/release/SKILL.md Step 7: the 4-step fallback chain for resolving the installed/cache root is operator-facing prose that must produce a correct CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT for every install topology. Verify the plan addresses the case where the CURRENT_VERSION cache dir does not exist at release time (e.g., the cache was pruned or the version variable is unset mid-step). Check whether the fallback to 'an existing valid larch-local cache version dir only if it is unambiguous' is adequately specified — what defines ambiguity, and what happens when two cached versions remain after a failed prune. Confirm the plan documents how CURRENT_VERSION is known inside the release step and whether it reliably matches the directory that was just written at release time. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: hook-probe-completeness
archetypes.rationale: The SessionStart probe must remain fail-open under set -euo pipefail with a stripped PATH; any missing guard in the plan could abort the hook or produce a corrupt advisory message.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit the sessionstart probe plan in scripts/sessionstart-health.sh and scripts/test-sessionstart-health.sh for completeness of its safety-isolation requirements. Check that every guard listed in the plan (empty HOME, missing .git, larch-logs present, missing lib, missing normalize_sparse_dirs, empty compare inputs) has a matching test case in the test-extension plan, not merely in the prose description. Verify the plan's set+e/restore isolation is sufficient when the outer script runs under set -euo pipefail, and that sourcing lib-sparse-dirs.sh with stderr suppressed and || true still leaves normalize_sparse_dirs bound on success but unbound on failure so the declare -F guard fires correctly. Confirm the probe is cwd-independent and never writes to or mutates the marketplace state even when intermediate commands produce unexpected output. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
